svg.aria-label: Diagram: Bedrock Web Search domain filtering shapes which results ground a model's answer, while a separate pair of settings decides whether the external web is reached at all. Domain filtering takes up to 100 allowed_domains or up to 100 blocked_domains on the filters parameter of the web_search tool, alongside optional user location parameters. Search is always served from the Amazon Bedrock web index. Fetch uses the Bedrock cache only when external_web_access is false, and reaches the external web only on a cache miss when the parameter is true and the bedrock-websearch:ExternalWebAccess IAM permission is granted. External retrieval takes effect only when both the permission is granted and the parameter is enabled. AWS notes that setting external_web_access to true introduces data exfiltration risk, since an agent could encode query data into a URL, and recommends setting it to false when working with sensitive data.
svg.title: The filter shapes the grounding; a different pair decides the boundary
svg.text: Two new controls on the results. Two older ones on the boundary.
Web Search on AWS Bedrock — domain filtering and user location, on the web_search tool.
NEW — precision over “the results that ground a model’s response”
filters.allowed_domains up to 100 → “limit results to trusted sources”
filters.blocked_domains up to 100 → “exclude sources you don’t want”
Plus optional user location, for “location-dependent questions, such as regional availability or local services”.
SEARCH — never leaves AWS
“Search is always served from the Amazon
Bedrock web index.”
Returns titles, URLs and snippets from the index
and knowledge graph, for high-confidence facts.
FETCH — the only path outward
false → “uses the Amazon Bedrock cache only”
true → cache first, external web “only on a
cache miss”
“your request data may leave the AWS boundary”
The gate has two conditions, and AWS states it three times on one page
REQUEST external_web_access: true
IAM bedrock-websearch:ExternalWebAccess
“External retrieval takes effect only when you both grant the permission and leave the parameter enabled.”
So neither half acts alone — a platform team can hold one and an application team the other.
Why the allow-list is not the egress control
“setting external_web_access to true introduces data exfiltration risk. An agent could encode query data
into a URL and then attempt to fetch that URL from the external internet.”
AWS’s named remedy is the parameter: “When you work with sensitive data, set … to false”.
A domain list constrains what grounds the answer. It does not decide whether anything leaves.
Two things that cost an afternoon.
The tool is server-side, so it is unavailable on bedrock-runtime — call the Responses API on bedrock-mantle. And the
model “uses the tool only when it determines the tool is needed”, so a filter constrains a search, not a guarantee of one.
Note the policy names: the ReadOnly and FullAccess external-search policies “grant the same three Web Search actions”.
